Scenario 1: If a site has both HTTP and HTTPS with default HTTP (which is atypically since the NSA stuff, it's become a thing to default to https)

A lot of the time this is posted, there's a big flood of "about time" comments. But really, despite being terrible for the end user, Flash represented something truly great. Ten years ago it was easily the most sophisticated accessible tool for quickly throwing things (whether animation or games) online. Any pre-teen could use it at school or acquire it through elicit means. It provided a great interface for teaching artists how to animate and programmers how to code. If you look at the recently exploded indie game dev scene, I bet there would be a surprising number of content creators with their roots in Flash development (even if just in a pissabout way that led them to different things). Before the wave of game tools like GameMaker and Unity, it was a simple way to get a program to accept input and be published on the web, and I'm still not sure of an animation tool quite like it. On the consumer end, yes, there were big downsides and places where it certainly shouldn't have been used, but the plethora of flash game and animation portals that exist out there showcase a whole realm of budding talent that perhaps otherwise wouldn't have blossomed. Flash (specifically Macromedia's Flash) will always hold a treasured place in many hearts.
